title: Azure / Virtual Machines / Overview
description: Azure Virtual Machines (microsoft.compute/virtualmachines): subscription inventory from Azure Resource Graph and host-level platform metrics (availability, CPU, memory, CPU credits, disk, network) for one VM. No agent needed. Guest-level metrics (logical disk space, per-process data) need VM Insights / Azure Monitor Agent and are covered by the 'Azure / Insights / Virtual Machines by Resource Group' dashboard (link at the top). Managed by Terraform (azure-managed-grafana): edit dashboards/virtual-machines/virtual-machines-overview.json, not the dashboard in the UI. Changes made in Grafana are overwritten on the next apply.

panels.title: Troubleshooting - $resource
panels.description: Start here when something looks wrong: is the resource running, has an alert fired, what changed? Resource Graph data; it lags a few minutes behind Azure. Grafana's identity needs read access (Monitoring Reader) on the resource.

panels.title: State
panels.description: Current state from Azure Resource Manager. Green: running/ready. Red: stopped, deallocated, failed or disabled. Orange: anything else, e.g. updating or starting.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines' and resourceGroup =~ '$rg' and name =~ '$resource'
| project ['Power state'] = tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.displayStatus), ['Provisioning'] = tostring(properties.provisioningState)

panels.title: Open alerts
panels.description: Azure Monitor alerts fired on this resource and not closed (alerts are kept 30 days). History across resources: the bundled Azure / Alert Consumption dashboard.

azureResourceGraph.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tolower(tostring(e.targetResource)) == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource')
| where tostring(e.monitorCondition) == 'Fired' and tostring(e.alertState) != 'Closed'
| summarize ['Open alerts'] = count()

panels.title: Changes (time range)
panels.description: Resource Manager changes to this resource and its child resources in the time range (Resource Graph change history, kept 14 days). Details on the right.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| summarize Changes = count()

panels.title: What changed
panels.description: Latest Resource Manager changes in the time range: who changed what, with which operation, and which properties. A change just before a problem started is the first suspect.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| project Time = todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp),
          Change = tostring(properties.changeType),
          Resource = iff(target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource'), '(this resource)', substring(target, strlen(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/$resource')) + 1)),
          ['Changed by'] = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.changedBy),
          Operation = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.operation),
          Properties = strcat_array(bag_keys(properties.changes), ', ')
| order by Time desc
| take 50

panels.title: Virtual machines
panels.description: Number of VMs (microsoft.compute/virtualmachines) in the subscription. Source: Azure Resource Graph, all VMs in the selected subscription (not filtered by resource group).

azureResourceGraph.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'
| summarize VMs = count()

panels.title: Running
panels.description: VMs whose power state (properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code) is PowerState/running. Source: Azure Resource Graph, all VMs in the selected subscription (not filtered by resource group).

azureResourceGraph.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'
| where tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code) =~ 'PowerState/running'
| summarize Running = count()

panels.title: Stopped (still billed)
panels.description: VMs in PowerState/stopped: shut down but still allocated, so compute is still billed. Deallocate them to stop compute charges. Source: Azure Resource Graph, all VMs in the selected subscription (not filtered by resource group).

azureResourceGraph.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'
| where tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code) =~ 'PowerState/stopped'
| summarize Stopped = count()

panels.title: Deallocated
panels.description: VMs in PowerState/deallocated (no compute charges). Source: Azure Resource Graph, all VMs in the selected subscription (not filtered by resource group).

azureResourceGraph.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'
| where tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code) =~ 'PowerState/deallocated'
| summarize Deallocated = count()

panels.title: Virtual machines in subscription
panels.description: Inventory of all VMs in $sub from Azure Resource Graph. Power state comes from properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code (PowerState/ prefix removed). Click a VM name to show its metrics below; click a resource group to open the VM Insights dashboard for it.

azureResourceGraph.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'
| extend vmSize = tostring(properties.hardwareProfile.vmSize),
         osType = tostring(properties.storageProfile.osDisk.osType),
         powerState = tostring(split(tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code), '/')[1]),
         provisioningState = tostring(properties.provisioningState),
         zone = tostring(zones[0])
| extend powerState = iff(isempty(powerState), 'unknown', powerState),
         zone = iff(isempty(zone), '-', zone)
| project name, resourceGroup, location, vmSize, osType, powerState, provisioningState, zone
| order by resourceGroup asc, name asc

panels.title: VM availability
panels.description: VmAvailabilityMetric, aggregation Minimum (pinpoints any unavailability in the interval), last value. 1 = running and available, 0 = unavailable (stopped from inside the guest or rebooting). No value = unknown: a VM stopped or deallocated through Azure stops emitting the metric.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Percentage CPU (Average), last value. Red above 80 %.

panels.title: Available memory
panels.description: Available Memory Percentage (Average), last value. Host-side platform metric, no agent needed. Red below 10 %.

panels.title: CPU credits remaining (B-series)
panels.description: CPU Credits Remaining (Average), last value. Only B-series burstable VMs emit this metric; other sizes show no value. At 0 credits the VM is throttled to its baseline CPU.

panels.title: VM availability
panels.description: VmAvailabilityMetric. 'average' = share of each interval the VM was available; 'minimum' drops to 0 if it was unavailable at any time in the interval. Gaps = unknown (VM stopped/deallocated through Azure). The metric also has a Context dimension (Platform / Customer / Unknown), not split here.

panels.title: Percentage CPU
panels.description: Percentage CPU (Average): share of allocated compute units in use. Dashed lines at 70 % and 80 %.

panels.title: CPU credits (B-series only)
panels.description: CPU Credits Remaining and CPU Credits Consumed (Average). Only B-series burstable VMs emit these metrics; other sizes show no data.

panels.title: Available memory (bytes)
panels.description: Available Memory Bytes (Average): physical memory immediately available to processes. Host-side platform metric, no agent needed.

panels.title: Available memory (%)
panels.description: Available Memory Percentage (Average). Dashed lines at 20 % (warning) and 10 % (critical).

panels.title: Disk bytes read / written (all disks, per interval)
panels.description: Disk Read Bytes and Disk Write Bytes (Total): bytes moved across all disks per time grain. The grain grows with the time range, so values are per interval, not per second. For bytes/sec see the OS disk and data disk throughput panels.

panels.title: Disk operations/sec (all disks)
panels.description: Disk Read Operations/Sec and Disk Write Operations/Sec (Average).

panels.title: OS disk throughput
panels.description: OS Disk Read Bytes/sec and OS Disk Write Bytes/sec (Average).

panels.title: OS disk IOPS
panels.description: OS Disk Read Operations/Sec and OS Disk Write Operations/Sec (Average).

panels.title: OS disk queue depth
panels.description: OS Disk Queue Depth (Average): outstanding IO requests on the OS disk. A sustained high value with latency growth means the disk is saturated.

panels.title: OS disk IOPS / bandwidth consumed %
panels.description: OS Disk IOPS Consumed Percentage and OS Disk Bandwidth Consumed Percentage (Average): use of the OS disk's provisioned limits. Only on VM series that support premium storage. Not split by LUN: the OS disk is a single disk. Dashed lines at 80 % and 95 %.

panels.title: Data disk IOPS consumed % by LUN
panels.description: Data Disk IOPS Consumed Percentage (Average), split by LUN. Only on VM series that support premium storage; no data if the VM has no data disks. Dashed lines at 80 % and 95 %.

panels.title: Data disk bandwidth consumed % by LUN
panels.description: Data Disk Bandwidth Consumed Percentage (Average), split by LUN. Only on VM series that support premium storage; no data if the VM has no data disks. Dashed lines at 80 % and 95 %.

panels.title: Data disk throughput by LUN
panels.description: Data Disk Read Bytes/sec and Data Disk Write Bytes/sec (Average), split by LUN. No data if the VM has no data disks.

panels.title: Data disk IOPS by LUN
panels.description: Data Disk Read Operations/Sec and Data Disk Write Operations/Sec (Average), split by LUN. No data if the VM has no data disks.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: OS Disk Latency (Average) and Data Disk Latency (Average, split by LUN): average time to complete each IO.

panels.title: Network in / out (per interval)
panels.description: Network In Total and Network Out Total (Total): bytes received / sent on all network interfaces per time grain (grows with the time range). The deprecated billable metrics (Network In / Network Out) are not used.

panels.title: Inbound / outbound flows
panels.description: Inbound Flows and Outbound Flows (Average): number of current flows in each direction.

panels.title: Flow creation rate (max)
panels.description: Inbound Flows Maximum Creation Rate and Outbound Flows Maximum Creation Rate (Average).
